mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has collapsed from -13.4% to -23.6% in the most recent week, signaling a sudden shift to remote work or lockdown. This reduction in commuting activity will suppress retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks as fewer workers pass through commercial districts.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined 10.2 percentage points week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen steadily from 5.6% to 7.1% over four weeks, indicating sustained home-based activity preference. This behavioral shift away from out-of-home venues will continue to depress RETAIL_REC mobility over the next two weeks as the residential preference persists.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased monotonically from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility declines by more than 1 percentage point in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has deteriorated from -27.6% to -38.1% to -44.0% and partially recovered to -38.1%, indicating volatile outdoor recreation demand. When PARKS mobility falls below -40%, it signals weather or policy constraints that simultaneously suppress RETAIL_REC through reduced foot traffic in commercial precincts within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -40% in current week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -38.1% at t-0w, previously -44.0% at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the week following a PARKS reading below -40%, or PARKS recovers above -35% without corresponding RETAIL_REC decline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has remained severely depressed at -40% to -43% across all four weeks, indicating sustained public transport avoidance. This persistent transit collapse will interact with WORKPLACES decline to amplify RETAIL_REC suppression over the next four weeks, as both commuting and discretionary retail access are constrained.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases relative to the last 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain in the specified depressed ranges.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near baseline (0.6% to 1.0% in recent weeks) while RETAIL_REC remains deeply negative (-14.3% at t-0w). This divergence indicates consumers are prioritizing essential shopping over discretionary retail. If GROCERY_PHARM remains stable while RETAIL_REC is suppressed, the behavioral preference for essentials will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM within -1% to +2% AND RETAIL_REC below -10%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 1.0% vs RETAIL_REC at -14.3% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains stable, indicating a shift back to discretionary spending.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp WORKPLACES decline at t-0w (-23.6%, a 10.2 point drop) signals a policy intervention or lockdown announcement. Such interventions typically trigger a one-week lag before retail behavior fully adjusts. RETAIL_REC will decline further in week t+1w as the policy impact propagates through consumer behavior.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines more than 8 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -13.3% to -23.6% between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in week t+1w following the WORKPLACES shock, or WORKPLACES recovers by more than 5 percentage points without corresponding RETAIL_REC recovery.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has been consistently negative across all four weeks (-27.6% to -44.0%), indicating suppressed outdoor recreation. In regimes where outdoor activity is constrained, consumers may substitute toward indoor retail venues. If PARKS mobility begins to recover above -30%, RETAIL_REC will increase over the next four weeks as consumers shift from home-based to out-of-home activities.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases above -30% in any of the next two weeks
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above -30% but RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 5 percentage points over the following four weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite PARKS recovery.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has increased from 5.6% to 7.1% while TRANSIT has remained severely depressed at -43.0%, creating a regime where home-based activity dominates and public transport access is unavailable. This combination will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks because consumers lack convenient transit access to retail districts and prefer home-based activities.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 7.1% and TRANSIT at -43.0% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 6 percentage points over the next 28 days when RESIDENTIAL remains above 6% and TRANSIT remains below -40%.
